family: MOD3 zero-residue family defined in proof.md: for every n>=0 and x in {0,1}^n, f_n(x)=1 iff x_1+...+x_n is congruent to 0 modulo 3 (so f_0(empty)=1). The language L={x : the number of ones in x is divisible by 3} is decided by one fixed linear-time counting algorithm at every length; it is in P and hence in NP with the empty-witness verifier V(x,w)=1 iff w is empty and x is in L, witness bound W(n)=0. No advice, no per-length choices, and witnesses are not circuit inputs.
theorem: For this one fixed total uniform family and EVERY integer n>=2, every circuit in the full Li-Yang B2 model (all 16 binary gates, unrestricted fan-out and depth, repeated pins allowed, zero-cost inputs, wires, constant nodes and output selection, every gate counted) computing f_n has at least 2n-3 gates: C_B2(f_n)>=2n-3. Hence there exists N (N=2) with C_B2(f_n)>=2n-3 for every integer n>=N, and liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=2. Proof: self-contained Schnorr-type gate elimination with explicit normalization, in proof.md.
